points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, 1 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease.
points.textNote: KMCRIC gives the same tendon side (radial to the FCU tendon), the same reference (palmar wrist crease) and the same distance (1 cun proximal). Only the wording differs.
points.error: About 0.35 cun proximal to the pisiform-defined wrist crease (1.35 cun instead of 1 cun). Measured from the model's own HT7 marker it is 1.06 cun. Both are within the 0.5 cun tolerance.
points.basis: I measured along the forearm axis, using the elbow-to-wrist direction of the anterior crease markers: u ≈ (0.155, 0.972, -0.176), s = u·p. The radius runs from (-0.2345,1.059,-0.0229) to (-0.2773,0.8296,0.0178), so the forearm tilts about 10° forward. Cubital crease: LU5, PC3 and HT3 give s ≈ 1.009–1.013 (mean 1.011). Palmar wrist crease: the proximal border of the pisiform (pisiform maxY (-0.2357,0.8253,0.0318)) gives s = 0.760. LU9 gives s = 0.753 and PC7 s = 0.760. 12 cun = 0.251 m, so 1 cun = 0.0209 m. HT5 right (-0.2452,0.8569,0.0368) gives s = 0.788, which is 0.028 m (1.35 cun) above the crease; HT7 is at s = 0.766. x = -0.245 is about 0.8 cm radial to the pisiform's radial edge (minX -0.2409), so the marker is on the radial side of the FCU line. It sits over the radial half of the distal ulna (ulna minX -0.2481 at y 0.8415) on the anterior skin. In the skin, muscle and bone images, the gold dot is on the ulnar part of the anterior distal forearm, about 1.5 cm above where the hand widens and above the carpal bones. Left and right markers are symmetric. Side note: HT4 is only 0.29 cun above HT5, which compresses the HT4–HT5 spacing; HT4 itself was not reviewed here.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, 0.5 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease.
points.textNote: KMCRIC matches WHO: radial side of the FCU tendon, 0.5 cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 (p.85): On the anteromedial aspect of the wrist, radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, on the palmar wrist crease. Note: in the depression radial to the proximal border of the pisiform bone, on the palmar wrist crease.
points.textNote: KMCRIC ('radial to the radial border of the FCU tendon, on the palmar wrist crease') matches WHO. The shortLocation is a faithful abbreviation.
points.error: About 0.3 cun (6 mm) proximal to the proximal border of the pisiform, at the level of the distal end of the ulna. This is within an educational marker's precision.
points.basis: HT7 right (-0.247,0.835,0.0407) gives a forearm-axis s of 0.766. The pisiform proximal border (maxY (-0.2357,0.8253,0.0318)) gives s = 0.760 and the distal tip of the ulna (minY (-0.2368,0.8288,0.0126)) gives s = 0.767. The marker is therefore in the gap between the ulnar head and the pisiform, 0.006 m (0.29 cun at 0.0209 m/cun) proximal to the pisiform's proximal border. The other crease points are LU9 at s 0.753 and PC7 at s 0.760. Mediolaterally, the pisiform spans x -0.2324 to -0.2409 (FCU insertion) and the hook of the hamate is at maxZ_anterior (-0.2466,0.8144,0.0338). HT7 at x = -0.247 is just radial to the pisiform/FCU line and is not on the ulnar side of the tendon. In the bone image, the gold dot sits above and radial to the pisiform bulge at the proximal edge of the carpus. In the skin image, it is on the ulnar part of the wrist where the hand begins to widen. Left and right are symmetric.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: In the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fifth thoracic vertebra (T5), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior midline.
points.textNote: KMCRIC matches WHO exactly: T5 spinous process inferior border level, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior midline.
points.basis: The T5 (FMA9922) spinousLowerBorderY is 1.2789; the marker is at y 1.279, so the level is exact. Vertebral series check: C7 tip 1.3971, T1 1.3827, T2 1.3621, T3 1.3375, T4 1.318, T5 1.2879, T6 1.2463. The neighbouring markers BL14 (1.311 = T4 lower border 1.3112) and BL16 (1.2428 = T6 lower border 1.2428) follow the same rule. The posterior midline is at x ≈ 0 (spinous tips x within ±0.003). Lateral distance |x| = 0.038 is half of the second-line distance used for BL41–BL47 (|x| = 0.075). In the bone image, the BL44 dots at 0.075 lie at the medial borders of the scapulae, so 3 cun ≈ 0.075 and 1.5 cun ≈ 0.0375. The landmark file has no scapula, so this check comes from the image. A chest-based cun (ST17 at |x| 0.09 = 4 cun) would give 1.5 cun = 0.034, which is still within 0.2 cun. In the skin, muscle and bone images, the two gold dots are symmetric about the spine (56 px each side, versus 111 px for the BL44 dots), on the paravertebral muscle between GV line and second line, and at the level between BL14 and BL16.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 (p.226): On the upper abdomen, 6 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line.
points.textNote: KMCRIC matches WHO: upper abdomen, on the anterior median line, 6 cun above the centre of the umbilicus. The shortLocation is equivalent.
points.error: About 0.34 cun (8 mm) superior to the B-cun target y ≈ 1.152. Within tolerance. The upper CV series is placed as if the xiphisternal junction were at the CV16 marker (y 1.214) rather than at the lower end of the sternal body (y 1.2006).
points.basis: Umbilicus: CV8 at y 1.005. Xiphisternal junction: sternal body (FMA7487) minY 1.2006, and the xiphoid maxY is 1.2046. 8 cun = 0.1956 m, so 1 cun = 0.02445 m vertically, and 6 cun above CV8 gives y 1.1517. Measuring along the skin path through the CV8–CV16 markers gives y ≈ 1.154. The marker at (-0.0001,1.1601,0.1268) is 0.0084 m higher, about 0.34 cun. The marker is on the midline (x ≈ 0), 2.2 cm below the xiphoid tip (xiphoid minY 1.1825), on the linea alba below the infrasternal angle. This matches the bone and muscle images, where the gold dot is below the sternum and xiphoid, between the converging costal margins and above CV13/CV12. Consistency note: by this scale CV15 (1.1882) is at 7.49 cun and CV16 (1.2141) at 8.55 cun. The images show the CV16 dot about 1 cm above the lower end of the sternal body, which explains the slight upward bias. Caveat: in the skin image the visible navel depression is about 1–1.5 cm below the CV8 dot. If the true umbilical centre is lower, CV14 would be about 0.45–0.5 cun high, which is still borderline ok. Per the brief, CV8 was used as the umbilicus.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: In the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra (L2), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
points.textNote: KMCRIC (L2 spinous lower border level, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior midline) matches WHO. The point file has whoStandardPage = null, so no page was given.

GV4 [0, 1.017, -0.0877] sits at the same level on the midline. x = 0.038 from the midline. No scapula is in landmarks.json, so lateral scale comes from the 3-cun second-line markers at x 0.075 (BL52 at the same level is at -0.0746; SI14, 3 cun lateral to T1, is at -0.0711). That makes 1.5 cun about 0.037 m, and 0.038 matches. A rough cross-check from the anterior trunk (8 cun xiphisternal-umbilicus ~0.198 m, about 0.025 m/cun) gives the same. In the posterior skin, muscle and bone images, the gold dots sit symmetrically over the paraspinal (erector spinae) bulge, level with the L2 spinous process and lateral to the transverse-process line. They are also level with BL52 (지실) on the second line.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 p.137: On the posteromedial aspect of the ankle, in the depression between the prominence of the medial malleolus and the calcaneal tendon.
points.textNote: KMCRIC (안쪽복사 융기와 발꿈치힘줄 사이의 오목한 곳) matches WHO.
points.basis: Right marker [-0.0405, 0.0871, -0.0471], skin [-0.0435, 0.0871, -0.0471]. Tibia (FMA24477) minY, the medial malleolus tip, is at [-0.0562, 0.0733, -0.0322], so the prominence is ~1-1.5 cm above it at y ~0.085-0.088. The marker's y 0.0871 is at prominence level. In z, the marker is 1.5 cm behind the malleolus (z ~-0.032) and well in front of the posterior heel/tendon line (calcaneus minZ_posterior z -0.0873; talus posterior process z -0.0627). That puts it in the malleolus-tendon gap, at most ~0.3 cun anterior of the exact midpoint (estimated z ~-0.05 to -0.055). The Achilles tendon is not in the landmarks, so that midpoint is an estimate. The images (anterior-left oblique of both ankles) show the gold dot on the posteromedial ankle, just behind the malleolus and above 대종/수천. The view cannot show the tendon edge clearly, but nothing shows the dot in front of the malleolus or on the tendon.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the medial aspect of the foot, posteroinferior to the medial malleolus, superior to the calcaneus, in the depression anterior to the medial attachment of the calcaneal tendon.
points.textNote: KMCRIC (안쪽 복사 아래 뒤쪽, 발꿈치뼈 위쪽, 발꿈치힘줄 안쪽 부착부의 앞쪽 오목한 곳) matches WHO. The point file has no WHO page.
points.basis: Right marker [-0.0443, 0.0659, -0.0648], skin x -0.0473. Calcaneus (FMA24497) maxY is [-0.0834, 0.061, -0.0577] and its posterior surface (minZ) is z -0.0873. The marker is ~0.5 cm above the calcaneal upper border and roughly 1-2 cm in front of the tendon line at the heel back, i.e. in the pre-Achilles depression. It is posteroinferior to KI3 [-0.0405, 0.0871, -0.0471]: 2.1 cm lower and 1.8 cm posterior. In the oblique ankle images the gold dot sits just below and behind 태계 at the posteromedial heel, above the calcaneus. The tendon itself cannot be resolved in these views.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the medial aspect of the foot, 1 B-cun inferior to KI3, in the depression anterior to the calcaneal tuberosity.
points.textNote: Same location as WHO. KMCRIC adds a scaling rule not in WHO: take KI3-to-ground as 3 cun. On this body that cun is 0.029 m, against ~0.0235 m from the 13-cun leg B-cun, a ~6 mm difference. This is a measuring convention, not a different landmark.
points.basis: Right marker [-0.0395, 0.058, -0.040]; KI3 is at y 0.0871, z -0.0471. The marker is 0.029 m below KI3, exactly 1 cun under KMCRIC's rule (KI3 to sole ~0.087 m = 3 cun). With the leg B-cun (SP9 y 0.392 to malleolus prominence ~0.087 = 13 cun, 0.0235 m/cun), the target y is ~0.064, so the marker is ~0.25 cun lower. Either way it is within 0.5 cun. It is 7 mm (~0.3 cun) anterior of straight below KI3 (z -0.047). It stays in front of the calcaneal tuberosity (posterior calcaneus z -0.0873; medial process at [-0.0574, 0.0254, -0.0726]) and below and behind the malleolus tip [-0.0562, 0.0733, -0.0322]. On this model 1 cun below KI3 falls level with the medial talus (talus maxX [-0.0563, 0.0627, -0.046]) rather than on the calcaneus itself, which is a model-proportion limitation. In all three images the right-side gold dot is hidden behind the 수천/조해 labels; only the left-side dot at the medial heel is visible. The image check therefore rests mainly on the numbers.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 p.184: On the lateral abdomen, inferior to the free extremity of the 12th rib.
points.textNote: KMCRIC (옆배, 열두째 갈비뼈끝의 아래쪽) and the short text (열두째 갈비뼈 자유끝 아래) match WHO.
points.error: The marker sits above the free end of the 12th rib, not below it. It is about 2.3-2.8 cm (~1.1 cun) too superior. Its height is lateral to the 11th intercostal space and slightly above the 11th rib tip too. Its distance from the midline and its z are acceptable (lateral skin over the rib tip).
points.basis: Right 12th rib (FMA8533): minX [-0.0833, 1.0349, -0.037], minY [-0.0794, 1.0234, -0.0357], last anterior-arc point [-0.07, 1.0332, -0.0444]. The free end therefore centres at ~[-0.081, 1.03, -0.037] and its lowest edge is at y 1.0234. The marker's y of 1.046 is 1.6 cm above the tip centre and 2.3 cm above its lower edge. The point belongs just below the tip, at y ~1.015-1.02 (about level with L2 spinousLowerBorderY 1.017 / BL23). Scale: xiphisternal junction (sternal body minY 1.2006) to umbilicus (CV8 y 1.005) = 8 cun, 0.0245 m/cun, so the error is ~1.1 cun. Seen from the side, at y 1.046 the 11th rib (anterior arc [-0.09, 1.0729, -0.0437] → [-0.11, 1.0305, 0.0042]) is at z ~-0.013 and the 12th at ~[-0.066, z -0.046]. The marker projects between them, and the 11th rib tip (minY 1.0258, minX at y 1.037) is also below it. In the frontal bone image the gold dot sits at the outer edge of the lower costal arch, above the level where the lower ribs end, not under a rib tip. The suggestion keeps the current lateral skin depth (skin x ~-0.122, +3 mm marker offset) and z ~-0.043 lateral to the tip, and lowers y to 1.018. The left side mirrors this: [0.125, 1.018, -0.043].

points.whoLocation: On the posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 3 B-cun superior to the dorsal wrist crease.

It sits on the lateral-to-anterolateral surface, in front of the forearm's most lateral point and in front of the brachioradialis tendon, not on the posterolateral aspect. Its neighbours LI5 (dorsoradial) and LI7 (posterolateral) both lie behind it, so LI6 breaks the line.

Marker y 0.8903, surface 0.8899: OK. Side: skin ray-casts at y 0.8895 put the lateral extreme at x −0.2749, z 0.005–0.010, with the posterolateral skin at (−0.2712, −0.005) and (−0.2685, −0.010). Marker surfacePoint (−0.2737, z 0.0124) lies anterior to the lateral extreme. Muscle sections at y 0.89: brachioradialis z 0.0012..0.0092; ECRL z −0.0040..0.0015; ECRB z −0.0070..−0.0034; APL z −0.0143..−0.0063. Radius FMA23464 is centred near (−0.257, −0.001), so the marker lies anterolateral to the bone. Interpolating along the skin between LI5 (z 0.0081, dorsoradial snuffbox) and LI7 (z −0.0123) gives z ≈ −0.004 at this height. In the posterior-view images the LI6 dot sits on the lateral silhouette edge, while LI7 sits on the posterior face. The suggestion is the skin point; the 3 mm-lifted marker would be ≈[-0.274, 0.8895, -0.0065]. The left side [0.2756, 0.8901, 0.0132] mirrors the same offset.

points.whoLocation: On the upper abdomen, 2 B-cun lateral to the centre of the umbilicus.
points.textNote: KMCRIC '윗배, 배꼽의 중심에서 가쪽으로 2寸' matches WHO, which also places it on the 'upper abdomen'.
points.error: Measured against CV8, the marker is exact: same y 1.005, 5.0 cm lateral = 2.2 cun from ST17 at x 0.09 = 4 cun. But the umbilicus modelled on the skin is a pit centred at y ≈0.990 on the midline, 1.5 cm (≈0.6 cun) below CV8/ST25, so the marker sits visibly above the navel. The error comes from CV8's level. Other umbilicus-level markers keyed to y 1.005 (KI16 and SP15 in landmarks.json) share it.
points.basis: Ray-casting skin.glb on the anterior midline gives a 6 mm-deep pit with z min 0.1065 at (x 0, y 0.990). The pit spans y 0.981–0.996 and is flanked by z ≈0.112–0.117. At y 1.005 (CV8) the midline skin is smooth (z 0.1129). In the skin image the navel shows about 25 px (≈1.7 cm at 14.8 px/cm, from the 10 cm gap between the ST25 dots) below the two gold dots. A cross-check with B-cun supports y 0.990: with the navel there, xiphisternal junction (sternal body minY 1.2006) to navel = 2.63 cm/cun and navel to the pubic symphysis top (CV2 0.8479) = 2.84 cm/cun. With CV8 1.005 those become 2.45 vs 3.14. Lateral distance is fine: 0.05 m against 2 cun = 0.045 m from ST17. The suggested skin z at (−0.05, 0.990) is 0.1113, plus the 3 mm lift = 0.1143. If CV8 is kept as the umbilicus by convention, this point is ok relative to it.

Numbers: ST17 x=-0.090 (4 cun) gives 6 cun = 0.135. 1st ICS from bone.glb anterior sections: 1st costal cartilage lower edge y 1.335 (x=-0.03) and 1st rib lower edge 1.344 (x=-0.05); 2nd costal cartilage upper edge 1.317 (x=-0.02 to -0.04) and 2nd rib upper edge 1.321 (x=-0.05). The ICS spans about 1.317-1.341, centre about 1.328. Landmarks agree: rib1 anteriorArc y 1.3462 and rib2 y 1.3051 at x=-0.05. Skin front surface at (-0.135, 1.328) is z=0.0403 by skin.glb ray, plus the 3 mm marker offset. Note: CV20 1.3164, KI26 1.3155 and ST14 1.3149 use the same low 1st-ICS convention.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the anterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LU5 with LU9, 7 B-cun superior to the palmar wrist crease.

points.whoLocation: In the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the twelfth thoracic vertebra (T12), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior midline.

Images: both gold dots sit over the erector spinae, just lateral to the tip of the L1 transverse process (|x| 0.0366, y 1.0775), with left and right symmetric (z -0.0929 and -0.0934).

points.whoLocation: On the posterior aspect of the wrist, in the depression ulnar to the extensor digitorum tendon, on the dorsal wrist crease.

The marker may be 3-5 mm radial of the ED/EDM gap (estimated just over the distal radioulnar joint at x about -0.249). points.whoLocation: On the posterior aspect of the forearm, midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and the ulna, 2 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease.
points.textNote: KMCRIC gives the same location: midpoint between the ulna and radius, 2 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease. Its note that PC6 is the anterior counterpart is an editorial addition and does not change the location.
points.error: The marker is about 1.1 cm (about 0.5 cun) too proximal; this is borderline between minor and ok. It sits 2.5 cun above the dorsal wrist crease instead of 2 cun. Its side-to-side position, in the radius-ulna gap, is correct.
points.basis: Forearm cun: the cubital crease is at y about 1.075 (LU5 1.075, PC3 1.0771, HT3 1.075; humeral lateral epicondyle y 1.078). The dorsal wrist crease is at 0.827-0.830 (TE4 0.8271, LI5 0.828, styloid tips 0.8288/0.8296). 12 cun = 0.245-0.248 m, so 1 cun is about 0.0205 m. Other markers on the same forearm fit this scale: LI6 at 0.8903 is 3.0 cun above LI5, LI7 at 0.931 is 5.0 cun above it, and TE9 at 0.9675 is about 5 cun below the olecranon prominence (y about 1.06-1.065). The marker gap TE5 minus TE4 is 0.8793 - 0.8271 = 0.052 m = 2.5 cun, so the correct level is 0.8271 + 0.041 = 0.868. If the crease is taken at 0.830 instead, the error is 0.4 cun. Side to side: in the bone close-up the dot projects into the gap between the radius and the ulna. Shaft interpolation puts the gap midpoint at x about -0.248 to -0.251. z is interpolated along the dorsal skin between TE4 (z -0.0035) and TE5 (z -0.0212). PC6 (0.8799) sits equally high, so moving TE5 alone would break the KMCRIC TE5-PC6 correspondence.

points.whoLocation: On the posterior aspect of the forearm, 3 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease, on the radial border of the ulna.
points.textNote: KMCRIC '자뼈의 바로 노쪽' (immediately radial to the ulna) is the same as WHO 'on the radial border of the ulna'. The distance, 3 cun, also matches.
points.error: The marker is about 1.3 cm (about 0.6 cun) too proximal. It sits 3.6 cun above the dorsal wrist crease instead of 3 cun. Its side-to-side position, on the radial border of the ulna and ulnar to TE6, is correct. TE6, at the same y 0.902, is high by the same amount.
points.basis: Forearm scale as for TE5: 1 cun is about 0.0205 m, from the cubital crease at y about 1.075 (LU5, PC3, HT3; lateral epicondyle 1.078) to the dorsal crease at about 0.827 (TE4 0.8271, styloid tips 0.8288/0.8296). The marker gap TE7 minus TE4 is 0.902 - 0.8271 = 0.075 m = 3.6 cun, so the correct level is 0.8271 + 0.0615 = 0.888. Using 0.830 as the crease, the error is still 0.5 cun. Side to side: interpolating the ulna shaft from the olecranon (x about -0.207, y about 1.06; ulna maxY 1.0764) to the ulnar head (x about -0.240, y about 0.845; head radial edge -0.2481) puts the shaft axis at about -0.232 at y 0.89. The radial border is then about -0.238, and the marker's x of -0.239 fits. It is also 0.9 cm ulnar to TE6 (-0.248) at the same level, which is the correct relation. In all three close-ups the gold dot is mostly hidden behind the TE6 and TE7 labels, so I judged the side-to-side position from the numbers only. z is interpolated along the dorsal skin between TE5 (z -0.0212) and TE7 (z -0.0297).

points.whoLocation: On the lower abdomen, 2 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line.
points.textNote: KMCRIC gives the same location: on the anterior midline, 2 cun below the centre of the umbilicus.

The right hip bone's most medial point, at y 0.8193, is the middle of the symphysis surface, and in the bone close-up the CV2 dot sits at the top of the symphysis. 5 cun = 0.157 m, so 1 cun is 0.0314 m and CV5 should be at 1.005 - 0.0629 = 0.942. The marker is at 0.940 (2 mm off), at x = 0, on the skin (z 0.1208). Its neighbours are consistent: CV6 0.958 (1.5 cun), CV4 0.907 (target 0.911), CV3 0.8749 (target 0.879). Caveat: in the skin close-up, the rendered navel dimple appears about 24 px (about 1.7 cm) below the CV8 dot, which puts it at about y 0.988-0.99 by the CV8-CV2 image scale. If that is taken as the umbilicus, CV5 should be at about 0.932 and the marker is about 0.8 cm (about 0.3 cun) high, which is still within ok. The CV8 placement may be worth re-checking separately.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: In the sacral region, at the same level as the second posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 B-cun lateral to the median sacral crest. (The point file gives no WHO page.)
points.textNote: KMCRIC names the same level (2nd posterior sacral foramen) and the same distance, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest. No real difference.

Below 0.845 the bone narrows to coccyx width, which supports this numbering. BL27 (y 0.913) sits on the S1 pit, which fits. The rib-free back cun is 3 cun = 0.075, so 1.5 cun = 0.0375. Skin first hit at (-0.038, 0.898) is z -0.1187; I added the 3 mm marker offset. Images: in the skin, muscle and bone views the gold dots sit slightly below the 차료 (BL32) dots. Ligaments cover the sacrum in the bone view, so the foramina cannot be seen and the level rests on the mesh. Uncertainty is about ±0.5 cm because the mesh is low-poly.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the posterolateral aspect of the leg, between the inferior border of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius muscle and the calcaneal tendon, at the same level as 7 B-cun superior to BL60 (about 1 B-cun inferolateral to BL57).

Prominence of the lateral malleolus = most lateral distal fibula vertices (x -0.1124) at y 0.066-0.072, so about 0.069; the tip is fibula minY 0.0539. 16 cun = 0.360 m, so 1 cun = 2.25 cm, and 7 cun above the prominence = y 0.2265. The BL60 marker (y 0.086) sits about 1.7 cm above the prominence. Counting 7 cun from BL60 gives 0.236, so the marker only looks right because BL60 itself is high. Lateral gastrocnemius head (muscle.glb FMA45960): lowest vertex y 0.2135; at y 0.23 it spans x -0.108 to -0.083 and at y 0.24 x -0.115 to -0.088. Its inferolateral border near x -0.108 is about y 0.23, and the calcaneal tendon top is y 0.2377. Skin first hit at (-0.107, 0.227) is z -0.0964; I added the 3 mm offset.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the dorsum of the foot, distal to the anterior border of the lateral malleolus, posterior to the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal bone, in the depression inferior to the cuboid bone.
points.textNote: KMCRIC has the same four landmarks (anterior border of the lateral malleolus, distal; posterior to the 5th metatarsal tuberosity; inferior to the cuboid; depression). No real difference.

It is 1.2 cm anterior to the 5th metatarsal tuberosity tip (z -0.0122) and about 1.1 cm above the cuboid's lateral-most point (y 0.0355). In the mesh the cuboid's lower lateral edge at z -0.010 to -0.015 is y about 0.028-0.030. The lateral malleolus anterior border is z about -0.035. So the target lies between z -0.0216 and -0.012, posterior to the tuberosity, just below the cuboid at y about 0.027. Skin first hit along +x at (y 0.027, z -0.017) is x -0.1223; I added the 3 mm offset. points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 p.132: On the lateral aspect of the foot, distal to the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal bone, at the border between the red and white flesh.

At z 0.0777 it is past the 5th metatarsal head (z 0.0592), level with the little-toe proximal phalanx (z 0.0546-0.0806). At x -0.1115, y 0.030 it is on top of the forefoot over the 4th MTP region (4th metatarsal head [-0.1174, 0.0193, 0.0713]), about 3.5 cm medial to the lateral skin border at that z (x -0.147). That is the BL65/BL66 area, not BL64.

Little-toe phalanges (bone.glb) span z 0.0546-0.0948. A ray down through x -0.1115, z 0.0777 hits the top of the forefoot skin at y 0.0286, just under the marker. Red-white border just distal to the tuberosity: the lateral-most skin vertex near z 0.01 is [-0.1359, 0.0188, 0.0119], and the skin hit along +x at (y 0.019, z 0.011) is x -0.1355; I added the 3 mm offset. Images: in the skin, muscle and bone views the gold dot is at the forefoot near the base of the toes, just behind the 속골/지음 dots and well below the 금문 (BL63) dot, not at the tarsometatarsal junction.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 p.221: On the lower abdomen, 4 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line.
points.textNote: KMCRIC says the same: anterior midline, 4 cun below the centre of the umbilicus.
points.error: No real error. The marker is about 1.3 cm (about 0.35 cun) above the ideal level measured from the bony symphysis, which is within tolerance. It is on the midline (x 0).

Upper border of the pubic symphysis = highest right hip-bone vertex within 1.4 cm of the midline, y 0.8266 (bone.glb FMA16586; the landmark's medial point maxX is at y 0.8193, mid-symphysis). 5 cun = 0.178 m, so 1 cun = 3.57 cm, and 4 cun below the umbilicus = y 0.862. Marker y 0.8749 is +1.3 cm. If the model's CV2 marker (y 0.848) is taken as the border, the ideal is y 0.879 and the marker is 0.4 cm low. Either way it is within 0.5 cun. Images: the gold dot is on the linea alba midline between 관원 (CV4) and 곡골 (CV2), about 1 cun above the pubic crest in the bone view.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: In the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the tenth thoracic vertebra (T10), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
points.textNote: KMCRIC gives the same landmark (inferior border of the T10 spinous process) and the same distance (1.5 cun lateral to the posterior midline). Only the wording differs.
points.basis: The T10 spinousLowerBorderY is 1.1313 and the marker is at y=1.131, the same level as GV7 (midline below T10, y=1.131). The marker is 0.038 m from the midline. The 3-cun second bladder line on this model (BL46 x=-0.075, BL47 x=-0.0748, BL48 x=-0.075) puts 1.5 cun at about 0.0375 m. In the bone image the second-line dots sit at about the medial scapular border, and the BL19 dots sit about halfway between them and the spinous processes. points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 (p.183): In the anterior thoracic region, in the seventh intercostal space, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
points.textNote: KMCRIC gives the same space (7th intercostal) and the same distance (4 cun lateral to the anterior midline).
points.basis: Lateral distance: the marker is at x=-0.0899, on the nipple line (ST17 x=-0.09, which is 4 cun). Level: at x=-0.09 the right rib 4 anterior arc is at y=1.2541 and rib 5 at y=1.2114, so the 4th intercostal space is about 1.233 (ST17 is at 1.235). Rib 6 is at 1.1817 (its bony end has minY 1.1679 at x=-0.0919), giving a 6th space of about 1.168 (LR14, the 6th-space point, is at 1.169). The bony end of rib 7 is at x about -0.108 to -0.110, y 1.135 to 1.149 (anterior arc point 1.1487). The bony end of rib 8 is at x about -0.111 to -0.115, y 1.100 to 1.114 (anterior arc point 1.1136). So at x=-0.11 the 7th intercostal space lies at about 1.12 to 1.135, and because the 7th and 8th costal cartilages rise medially it lies at about 1.13 to 1.145 at x=-0.09. The marker at y=1.142 is in the upper part of that space, about 2.7 cm (one rib space) below LR14. On this model 1 anterior-trunk cun = (1.2006-1.005)/8 = 0.0245 m, so the marker is within about 0.3 cun of the space centre. In the bone close-up the dot sits just medial to and below the bony end of rib 7, above the costal margin. Limitation: costal cartilages are not in the landmark data, so the cartilage course at x=-0.09 is interpolated.

points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the fibular aspect of the leg, anterior to the fibula, 7 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus. GB35 (posterior to the fibula) is at the same level.
points.textNote: KMCRIC matches WHO: fibular aspect of the leg, anterior to the fibula, 7 cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus.
points.error: The marker is about 1.5 to 2 cun (3.3 to 4.1 cm) too proximal. At y=0.269 it is about 8.8 cun above the lateral malleolus prominence. That puts it above the 8-cun midpoint of the popliteal crease to malleolus line (about 0.25) and above the ST40 marker (8 cun, y=0.2391), when it should be 1 cun below that midpoint. It is also 2.5 cm above GB35 (y=0.244), which WHO places at the same level. Lateral malleolus: the fibula tip (minY) is at y=0.0539, and the malleolar body is at about 0.076 to 0.079 (fibula minZ_posterior y=0.0757, maxX y=0.0793). That puts the prominence at about 0.072. 16 cun = 0.357 m, so 1 cun = 0.0223 m and 7 cun lies at 0.072 + 0.156 = 0.228. If the BL60 level (0.086) is taken as the prominence instead, 7 cun is at 0.236 and the marker is still 1.5 cun high. The fibula shaft at this level is at about x -0.113, z -0.041 (interpolated from the head near x -0.12, y 0.39 to the malleolus near x -0.105, z -0.047). The suggested point therefore keeps z at about -0.015, anterior to the fibula, with x on the lateral skin (between the GB37/GB36 marker contour, about -0.124 at z -0.012, and GB35, x -0.138 at z -0.029). In the frontal close-ups the gold dot sits at the lateral leg outline above the GB35 label, lateral to the fibula strip in the bone image, about a third of the way from the knee joint line to the ankle. points.whoLocation: WHO 2008: On the fibular aspect of the leg, anterior to the fibula, 5 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus.

points.basis: Same proportional frame as GB36. Popliteal crease: BL40 y=0.429. Lateral malleolus prominence: about 0.072 (fibula tip minY 0.0539; malleolar body about 0.076 to 0.079). 1 cun = 0.357/16 = 0.0223 m, so 5 cun lies at 0.072 + 0.112 = 0.184. With the prominence at 0.086, 5 cun is at 0.193 and the marker is still about 0.95 cun high. The fibula at y=0.18 to 0.21 is at about x -0.110 to -0.111, z -0.042 to -0.044, so z of about -0.015 on the lateral skin stays anterior to the fibula. The skin x follows the GB38/GB39 markers (x -0.1156 at y 0.1904; x -0.110 at y 0.1658). points.whoLocation: WHO 2008 (p.191): On the anterolateral aspect of the ankle, in the depression lateral to the tendon of the extensor digitorum longus, anterior and distal to the lateral malleolus.
points.textNote: KMCRIC matches WHO: anterolateral ankle, lateral to the extensor digitorum longus tendon, in the depression anterior and distal to the lateral malleolus.
points.error: The marker is on the anterolateral slope of the lateral malleolus itself, about 1 cm above its tip, not in the depression anterior and distal to it.
